item.title: #3586217: Remove the Search module
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 165 files, +7/−17141 · txt +6/−343 · php +1/−15826 · json +0/−1 · yml +0/−798 · twig +0/−173
  • Diff: 64a266a
  • Discussion: #3586217 · 5 contributors · 15 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

The Search module has been removed from Drupal core. This includes the /search routes and controller, the "Search form" block, the search page entity type and its admin UI, the node/user/help search plugins, the search index tables, and the Views integration (search argument, filter, sort, and row plugins) that shipped with the module. Site owners who use core's built-in keyword search need to install the contrib Search module before upgrading to keep this functionality; running update.php with search still enabled will show a warning that the module was removed from core. This follows Drupal's policy of moving lightly maintained core modules to contrib, the same path taken by HAL, RDF, and others (see the deprecated/removed modules list at drupal.org/node/3223395#s-search).

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: Sites with the search module still enabled will see an update.php requirements warning telling them the module was removed from core.
  • Deprecation: The core Search module (including its search_node, search_user, search_help, and search_embedded_form/other test submodules) is removed entirely; a contrib Search module should be installed as a replacement.

Technical details

The commit deletes core/modules/search in its entirety, roughly 17,000 lines: the SearchPage config entity, SearchPageRepository, SearchIndex/SearchQuery/ViewsSearchQuery, the SearchPluginBase/SearchPluginManager plugin system (#[Search] attribute), SearchController, the admin forms, the search_form_block block plugin, the search.page.* and search.settings config schemas, and the bundled search_node, search_user, search_help, and search_embedded_form submodules along with all their tests.

Outside the module directory the change is intentionally narrow: search is added to SystemRequirements::DRUPAL_CORE_REMOVED_MODULE_LIST in core/modules/system/src/Install/Requirements/SystemRequirements.php so SystemRequirementsHooks can surface an update-time warning on sites that still have it enabled, SchemaCheckTrait drops its now-unneeded search.page.*/search.settings ignored-property-path entries, and the core_fake/CoreFakeWithAllCustomClasses test database drivers drop their SearchQuery/ViewsSearchQuery subclasses. core/.phpstan-baseline.php and .deprecation-ignore.txt are pruned of search-specific entries. The removal was postponed until after #3595089 (Olivero theme removal) since Olivero contained search-specific markup and test coverage that would otherwise have failed.

Upgrade

Before upgrading a site that uses core search:

  1. Install the contrib Search module (or another search solution) to replace the functionality.
  2. Any custom code implementing \Drupal\search\Plugin\SearchInterface / extending SearchPluginBase, or referencing \Drupal\search\SearchPageRepositoryInterface, SearchIndex, SearchQuery, or the search.page.*/search.settings config, needs to be ported to the contrib module's equivalents.
  3. Views using the core views.argument.search, views.filter.search, views.field.search_score, views.sort.search_score, or views.row.search_view plugins will need to be rebuilt against contrib alternatives.

item.title: #3595089: Remove the Olivero theme
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main

  • Diff: 8d87e80
  • Discussion: #3595089 · 5 contributors · 21 comments
  • Followers: 6

Summary

The Olivero theme, one of Drupal's bundled front-end themes since Drupal 9, has been removed from core. It continues to exist as a standalone contrib project for sites that still want to use it. Sites currently running Olivero as their default (or admin) theme need to download and install the contrib version before upgrading to Drupal 12, otherwise the theme and its assets, templates, and configuration will simply disappear.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: The olivero theme is removed from Drupal core entirely; sites using it as their default or admin theme must install it as a contrib project (https://www.drupal.org/project/olivero) before upgrading to Drupal 12.

Technical details

The commit deletes the entire core/themes/olivero directory (templates, PHP preprocess classes, CSS/PCSS source, fonts, images, config schema, and default block/date-format config that ships with the theme), along with everything in core that referenced it: the MAINTAINERS.txt credit section, core/phpstan-baseline.neon ignore rules scoped to Olivero classes, the cspell dictionary entries for "olivero"/"olivero's", and the themes/olivero/fonts/** exclusion in .cspell.json. It also removes the Nightwatch tests in core/modules/search that depended on olivero_test and on installing Olivero as the default theme, since that test coverage is now maintained in the contrib Search project instead.

This is a pure "task: remove the theme" commit; it does not touch the codebase in a way that changes any public API or theme system hook. Related follow-up work (removing Olivero references from database dump fixtures, tracked in #3623927) was landed just before this commit so the removal wouldn't break other test suites. A later merge request (!17186) was opened right after this commit to add the olivero theme to Drupal core's list of formally removed extensions in system.install, which triggers a requirements warning for sites still running it after upgrade; that addition was not part of what shipped here.

Upgrade

Sites whose system.theme configuration (or admin theme) is set to olivero should, before upgrading to Drupal 12:

  1. Download and install the contrib Olivero project: https://www.drupal.org/project/olivero
  2. Confirm the site's default/admin theme still resolves correctly after the core removal.

No API changes are involved; this is purely the loss of a bundled theme.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: June 10, 2026
  • Committed: September 18, 2026 (3 months later)

Key contributors

  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)

Collaboration

catch noted that removing Olivero ahead of removing the core Search module was acceptable even though Search still referenced it ("I think we can remove Olivero with the references from search module still in search, since we know we're going to remove that too... it's OK if contrib search/olivero integrate"), and opened #3623927 to cover the remaining database-dump references. When Nightwatch tests relying on olivero_test kept failing, gábor hojtsy confirmed in Slack that the contrib Search module's own Nightwatch tests already passed, which let quietone and catch agree to simply delete the Olivero-dependent tests here rather than combine the Olivero and Search removal issues, which catch felt "would be harder to follow in git history."

item.title: #3623097: Remove remaining Gin and Claro implementation names from Default Admin theme, part 2
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 26 files, +129/−74 · php +109/−4 · json +16/−41 · css +3/−3 · yml +1/−1 · svg +0/−21 · md +0/−4
  • Diff: 67b98c1
  • Discussion: #3623097 · 6 contributors · 22 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 6 contributors

Summary

This is a follow-up cleanup of Drupal core's new, still-experimental "Default Admin" theme (forked from Gin/Claro), removing leftover references to the old "Gin" and "Claro" project names. The theme's "Focus color" setting previously stored the values gin and claro for its default and legacy-green presets; these are now named default and legacy_green. Existing sites with a saved focus color preference are updated automatically, no manual action is required for the common case, but the underlying stored value and the HTML attribute it produces have changed names. Several leftover icon files and a stale README that were copied from Claro's source tree were also removed from core, since the theme now either shares images with other components or no longer needs them.

Impact

Affects front-end developers and site owners.

  • Config change: Default Admin theme's preset_focus_color setting values renamed: gin to default, claro to legacy_green; existing stored config and per-user overrides are migrated automatically by a new post_update hook.
  • Theme change: The data-admin-focus HTML attribute now uses default/legacy_green instead of gin/claro, so custom CSS targeting the old attribute values or [data-admin-focus="claro"]/[data-admin-focus="gin"] selectors must be updated.

Technical details

The Settings::getSettingsForm() select options for preset_focus_color were renamed from gin/claro to default/legacy_green, and the CSS selectors in accent.css/accent.pcss.css were updated from [data-admin-focus="claro"] to [data-admin-focus="legacy_green"] (the gin value already mapped to the default preset and needed no selector change). A new default_admin.post_update.php adds default_admin_post_update_rename_focus_color_presets(), which rewrites the default_admin.settings config and any per-user overrides stored via user.data (in both the newer settings array format and the older flat key format) from the old gin/claro values to default/legacy_green. Coverage for this migration lives in the new FocusColorPresetUpdateTest kernel test.

Separately, several SVG icons and a README under images/core/ that were copied from Claro's source tree (and marked for removal once Claro moved into core) were deleted: one required-field icon moved into images/icons/ and is referenced from the compiled accent.pcss.css, and the remaining icons were dropped because equivalent images already exist elsewhere or are unused. The tests/fixtures/implementation-name-allowlist.json allowlist used by ImplementationNameTest was updated to drop entries for the removed claro references and add entries for the new post-update and test files, which still legitimately reference the old preset key names for migration purposes.

Upgrade

Custom subthemes or CSS overriding the focus color attribute should update selectors:

/* before */
[data-admin-focus="claro"] { ... }

/* after */
[data-admin-focus="legacy_green"] { ... }

Any custom code reading or setting the default_admin.settings:preset_focus_color config value or a user's default_admin user data directly should use default instead of gin and legacy_green instead of claro. Existing stored values are migrated automatically by default_admin_post_update_rename_focus_color_presets().

  • Committed: September 17, 2026 (2 days and 4 commits later)

item.title: #3623843: Remove Backbone.js and Underscore.js, not used in core anymore
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +0/−2243 · txt +0/−5 · js +0/−2176 · map +0/−2 · yml +0/−33 · json +0/−2 · lock +0/−25
  • Diff: 5b6a182
  • Discussion: #3623843 · 4 contributors · 20 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

Drupal core has removed the Backbone.js and Underscore.js third-party JavaScript libraries entirely. These were already marked internal-only and deprecated as of Drupal 10 (toolbar was the last core consumer of Backbone, and Underscore was only present as Backbone's dependency). Since Drupal 10 they carried no supported public API, but any contributed module or theme that still attached the core/internal.backbone or core/internal.underscore libraries, or otherwise relied on the global Backbone/_ objects being present, will now find them missing and must bundle their own copies.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: The internal.backbone and internal.underscore libraries, deprecated for external use since Drupal 10, are fully removed from core.libraries.yml and the core/assets/vendor directory; nothing in core ships or depends on Backbone.js or Underscore.js anymore.

Technical details

The change removes the internal.backbone and internal.underscore library definitions from core/core.libraries.yml, deletes the vendored core/assets/vendor/backbone and core/assets/vendor/underscore directories, and drops the corresponding COPYRIGHT.txt entries. It also removes backbone and underscore from core/package.json and core/yarn.lock, removes their asset-fetch entries from core/scripts/js/vendor-update.js (the script that downloads vendor JS during core releases), and drops the now-unused Backbone: 'readonly' global from core/eslint.config.mjs.

No core JavaScript referenced these libraries anymore at the time of removal (grepping the codebase before the patch turned up references only in the vendor files and library/config plumbing listed above), confirming the libraries were dead weight left over from the Drupal 10 deprecation.

Upgrade

Sites, modules, or themes that still declare a library dependency such as:

dependencies:
  - core/internal.backbone
  - core/internal.underscore

or otherwise expect the global Backbone or _ (Underscore) objects to be available because core loaded them, must now provide their own copies of Backbone.js and/or Underscore.js as third-party dependencies. Core no longer ships or loads these libraries.

  • Followers: 6

Summary

The Olivero theme, Drupal's default front-end theme since 9.4, is now formally marked as deprecated in core. This follows the separate policy decision to remove Olivero from core and move it to a contributed project. Sites currently using Olivero are not affected immediately: the theme still ships and works exactly as before. This issue just flips the deprecation flag and updates its tests accordingly; it does not remove any functionality. Site owners using Olivero should start watching the linked documentation page for the recommended migration path, since the theme will eventually be removed from core in a future release.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: The olivero theme is now marked lifecycle: deprecated in its .info.yml, pointing to https://www.drupal.org/node/3223395#s-olivero for migration guidance ahead of its eventual removal from core.

Technical details

The change adds lifecycle: deprecated and lifecycle_link: https://www.drupal.org/node/3223395#s-olivero to core/themes/olivero/olivero.info.yml, which is how Drupal core formally flags an extension as deprecated per the core deprecation policy (following the approval in the parent policy issue #3590816, referenced in the issue body).

Since flagging a theme as deprecated causes PHPUnit to emit deprecation notices when its code paths run, #[IgnoreDeprecations] was added to every test class that still exercises Olivero, both tests living inside the theme itself (OliveroTest, OliveroAvoidStorageUsingTest, OliveroMessagesTest, OliveroHexToHslTest) and core tests elsewhere that use Olivero as a fixture theme (e.g. BreadcrumbTest, NodeTitleTest, AjaxTest), so the test suite keeps passing without failing on the new deprecation notice. No PHP or Twig behavior in the theme itself was changed.

item.description:

  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 23 files, +135/−79 · php +37/−39 · yml +36/−35 · twig +33/−3 · css +27 · js +1/−1 · sql +1/−1
  • Diff: 91a722e
  • Discussion: #3582101 · 7 contributors · 25 comments
  • Followers: 9
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

As part of Claro's deprecation, Drupal core now ships new sites with the (experimental) Default Admin theme instead of Claro. The Standard installation profile and the Umami demo profile now install default_admin as their administration theme, and Standard also uses it as its default front-end theme. The core_recommended_admin_theme recipe and the standard recipe were updated the same way, so applying either to a site now sets up Default Admin rather than Claro. This only affects new installs or sites that explicitly apply these profiles/recipes; existing sites keep whatever admin theme they already have configured.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Standard and Umami install profiles, and the core_recommended_admin_theme/standard recipes, now set default_admin as the admin theme (and, for Standard, also as the default theme) instead of claro.

Technical details

The change swaps claro for default_admin throughout the profile and recipe config: system.theme.yml for standard, demo_umami, and nightwatch_a11y_testing, the themes: list in their .info.yml files, and the block config shipped for the admin theme (claro_login became default_admin_login, claro_help/claro_breadcrumbs/etc. became default_admin_*). The core_recommended_admin_theme recipe now installs default_admin and imports its blocks instead of Claro's, and standard recipe's system.theme action sets default: default_admin.

Because Default Admin doesn't render field wrapper classes the way Claro does (no .field--name-* markup), several functional tests that asserted on those classes (media library embed tests, standard profile tests, ImplementationNameTest) were rewritten to scope assertions to #block-default-admin-content and element selectors instead. A few Default Admin theme templates and styles were also adjusted to support being used this way: block--user-login-block.html.twig and a new user-login-block.css were added to render the login form without list markup, admin-toolbar-top-bar.html.twig gained role="region"/aria-label attributes, and the primary/secondary local-tasks templates now put the visually-hidden heading inside the <nav> element rather than before it.

item.title: #3612965: Allow Guzzle 8 in Drupal 11
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +131/−338 · php +87/−73 · lock +42/−257 · json +2/−8
  • Diff: 9df766b
  • Discussion: #3612965 · 5 contributors · 23 comments
  • Followers: 9
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Drupal core's composer.json now allows sites to install either Guzzle 7 or Guzzle 8 as the underlying HTTP client library, even though Drupal 11 itself continues to ship and be tested with Guzzle 7 by default. This backports the Guzzle 8 compatibility work originally done for Drupal 12 in #3612544, giving Drupal 11 site owners the option to move to Guzzle 8 in case Guzzle 7 reaches end of life before Drupal 11 does.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: guzzlehttp/guzzle constraint widened from ^7.10 to ^7.10 || ^8.0 (and guzzlehttp/psr7 to ^2.8.0 || ^3.0); Drupal 11 still ships and is tested with Guzzle 7 (bumped to 7.15.5) by default.

Technical details

The version constraints for guzzlehttp/guzzle and guzzlehttp/psr7 in core's composer.json were widened to ^7.10 || ^8.0 and ^2.8.0 || ^3.0 respectively, but composer.lock keeps the actually-installed version on Guzzle 7 (bumped to 7.15.5) rather than jumping to Guzzle 8, so nothing changes for sites that don't touch their own lock file.

To make Drupal's own code and test suite tolerate whichever version a site chooses, several compatibility shims were added: FileCookieJarShim now only defines its hardened backport of GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar when GuzzleHttp\ClientInterface::MAJOR_VERSION < 8, since Guzzle 8 ships that hardening natively, and its test skips itself under Guzzle 8. DrupalTestBrowser::doRequest() catches GuzzleHttp\Exception\BadResponseException instead of RequestException to match Guzzle 8's exception hierarchy. BrowserTestBase::loginHttps() falls back to parsing the raw Set-Cookie header via SetCookie::fromString() because Guzzle 8 no longer stores secure cookies received over the test's insecure HTTPS mock connection in its CookieJar. Kernel-test HTTP handler callables must now return a GuzzleHttp\Promise\PromiseInterface (via GuzzleHttp\Promise\Create::promiseFor()) instead of a bare Response, since Guzzle 8 changed the handler signature to ($request, array $options). A couple of assertions on Guzzle exception message text in UpdateAdvisoriesTest and UpdateFetcherTest were loosened to accept either the Guzzle 7 or Guzzle 8 message formatting. The php-http/guzzle7-adapter dev dependency was dropped.

Upgrade

No action is required for existing sites: Drupal 11 continues to lock to Guzzle 7 by default. Sites or modules that want to move to Guzzle 8 can now do so, since core's constraint permits it:

"guzzlehttp/guzzle": "^7.10 || ^8.0"

Run composer require guzzlehttp/guzzle:^8.0 to opt in. Code that directly catches GuzzleHttp\Exception\RequestException and expects it to cover bad HTTP responses should be aware Guzzle 8 uses GuzzleHttp\Exception\BadResponseException for that case.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 24, 2026
  • Committed: September 16, 2026 (1 month and 3 commits later)

Key contributors

  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • godotislate
  • daffie (Finalist)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

The initial commit landed the wrong merge request (MR 16839, which fully bumped composer.lock to Guzzle 8) instead of the intended MR 17094, which kept composer.lock on Guzzle 7 while allowing Guzzle 8. godotislate flagged the mistake in comment #16772202, and catch confirmed and corrected it: "Yes... got my tabs mixed up. Reverted the wrong MR, and committed the right one this time." godotislate also did the work of resolving merge conflicts and fixing test failures on the correct MR, tracing one remaining failure to an unrelated upstream issue (#3182064).

item.title: #2876298: Remove scaffolded csslint and eslint config
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 18 files, +0/−88 · md +0/−6 · json +0/−24 · txt +0/−1 · php +0/−12 · csslintrc +0/−37 · eslintignore +0/−8
  • Discussion: #2876298 · 16 contributors · 47 comments
  • Followers: 28
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 16 contributors

Summary

Drupal no longer scaffolds a .csslintrc, .eslintignore, or .eslintrc.json file into the root of every site built from drupal/core-composer-scaffold. CSSLint was replaced by stylelint back in 2017 (#2865971) and is considered dead, and the scaffolded ESLint config stopped working once core moved to ESLint v9 with a new config format (#3440225). Since using these tools requires manually installing ESLint/CSSLint plus the matching plugins anyway, and most real sites already keep their own lint configuration at the theme or repository root, core stops shipping these unused defaults into every install. This is a disruptive change targeted at Drupal 12.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Composer scaffold no longer copies .csslintrc, .eslintignore, or .eslintrc.json into the web root of new or updated Drupal sites.

Technical details

The fix removes the [web-root]/.csslintrc, [web-root]/.eslintignore, and [web-root]/.eslintrc.json entries from the drupal-scaffold file-mapping in core/composer.json (and the corresponding fixture composer.json files used by drupal-composer-scaffold tests), and deletes the source files themselves from assets/scaffold/files/ (csslintrc, eslintignore, eslintrc.json). Test fixtures and expectations across the scaffold plugin's test suite (e.g. ManageGitIgnoreTest, drush-style scaffold listing output) were updated to no longer expect these files to be copied or linked.

Core's own internal .eslintrc.json and .stylelintrc.json inside core/ are untouched. Only the copies that composer-scaffold writes out to the site's web root are removed, so core's own lint tooling and CI keep working; it is only external sites and themes that lose the auto-provisioned copy.

Upgrade

Sites that want to keep linting against core's rules must now do so manually, since the scaffolded copy is gone. Before this change, the scaffolded .eslintrc.json simply contained:

{
  "extends": "./core/.eslintrc.json"
}

Sites relying on this can recreate that file themselves (adjusting the relative path to core/.eslintrc.json if their web root differs), or point their own lint configuration directly at core's core/.eslintrc.json / core/.stylelintrc.json. There is no scaffolded .csslintrc replacement, since CSSLint itself is obsolete; use stylelint instead.

item.title: #3531854: Add a Design Tokens & CSS variables API
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 56 files, +4881/−0 · php +4664 · yml +215 · txt +2

Summary

Drupal core gains an experimental Design Tokens API, a standardized way to declare small, typed design values (dimensions, font families, font weights, numbers, typography) following the W3C Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) format, and to override their values per CSS selector "scope" (e.g. :root, .card) through a new design_token configuration entity. This follows the same front-end-friendly, YAML-plugin pattern already used by Single Directory Components and the Icon API, aiming to give contrib modules and Drupal themes a common vocabulary for CSS custom properties instead of everyone inventing their own. The API is explicitly marked experimental and not meant for production use yet: it defines the discovery and storage format, but does not yet include a mechanism for actually publishing the overridden values as page CSS, that is left for a follow-up. A new "Administer design tokens" permission controls who can manage the override entities, and existing sites get the new entity type automatically via a database update.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: system_update_12002() installs the new design_token config entity type on existing sites when they run database updates.
  • Permission change: New administer design tokens permission required to manage design_token config entity overrides.
  • New API: New design_token plugin type (*.tokens.yml discovery, W3C DTCG format) and design_token_value plugin type (Dimension, FontFamily, FontWeight, Number, Typography) for declaring design tokens, plus a new design_token config entity type for overriding token values by CSS selector scope.

Technical details

Tokens are discovered from {provider}.tokens.yml files (theme or module root) via YamlDiscovery inside the new DesignTokenPluginManager. Because DTCG data is a nested tree of groups and tokens (a token is any node containing a $value key), DesignTokenPluginManager::parseDtcg() walks the raw YAML into Group/DesignToken objects (both implementing DtcgInterface) and then flattenDefinitions() collapses that tree into flat plugin definitions keyed by dotted path (e.g. fontSize.small).

Each token's $value is resolved through a separate design_token_value plugin type (#[DesignTokenValue] attribute, discovered under Plugin/DesignTokenValue), which implements DesignTokenValueInterface::toDtcg()/toCss(). Core ships five initial value types: Dimension (restricted to px/rem per the current DTCG spec, though downstream code can subclass it to add units), FontFamily, FontWeight (accepts DTCG alias strings like bold/light via the FontWeightAlias enum), Number, and the composite Typography. Eight more DTCG types (color, shadow, gradient, etc.) are intentionally left for contrib and a later core proposal.

Value overrides live in the new design_token config entity (Drupal\Core\Theme\Entity\DesignToken), keyed by path/type, with a scopes map from CSS selector to a DesignTokenValuePluginCollection of typed values (dots in scope keys are escaped to % for config storage via getConfigScopeName()/getCssScopeName()). DesignToken::toCss() serializes a set of token entities into grouped inline CSS (selector{--name:value;}). A new CssSelector validation constraint blocks {, }, ; in scope keys to prevent CSS injection through stored config.

Upgrade

To declare theme or module design tokens, add a {provider}.tokens.yml file using the DTCG format, for example:

fontSize:
  small:
    "$type": dimension
    "$value":
      value: 12
      unit: px

To override a token's value for a given CSS selector, create a design_token config entity:

id: my_id
path: foo.bar.baz
type: dimension
scopes:
  ':root':
    value: 12
    unit: px

This API is experimental (@internal, "not meant for production use"): no publishing mechanism ships yet to turn overridden config entities into page CSS, and the value type list and validation are expected to change before stabilization.

Summary

Drupal now exposes the user entity's existing created field as a normal, configurable field on the "Manage display" page (hidden by default), and deprecates the old member_for extra field, scheduled for removal in Drupal 13. Sites that currently show "Member for" will keep showing it after upgrading to 11.5 or 12 (nothing changes visually), but a deprecation notice will appear whenever it renders, prompting site owners to switch their display configuration to the created field, which behaves like any other field and can be labeled, formatted, and themed normally. New installations have both fields hidden by default.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: The user entity's created field is now configurable on the user "Manage display" page (hidden by default); a post-update hook adds it as hidden to existing user displays.
  • Deprecation: The member_for user profile extra field is deprecated as of Drupal 11.5 and will be removed in Drupal 13; use the created field instead.

Technical details

In User::baseFieldDefinitions(), the created base field gained ->setDisplayOptions('view', ['region' => 'hidden'])->setDisplayConfigurable('view', TRUE), so it now appears on the user "Manage display" screen like any other field instead of being invisible to Field UI. UserHooks::userView() still builds the same hard-coded <h4 class="label"> render array for backward compatibility, but now wraps it in a #post_render callback, triggerMemberForDeprecation(), which raises an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice referencing the change record at https://www.drupal.org/node/3611943.

A new post-update function, user_post_update_add_created_to_display(), uses ConfigEntityUpdater to add created to the hidden section of every user entity view display that doesn't already define it, so upgrading sites gain the new field definition without any visible change. Default install profile displays (core.entity_view_display.user.user.*) now list both created and member_for under hidden and no longer include member_for under content. Drupal\user\UserListBuilder, used by the admin /admin/people listing, renamed its "Member for" table column key from member_for to created to match.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Sites and contrib/custom code that reference the member_for extra field (for example in EntityViewDisplay configuration, or custom code checking $display->getComponent('member_for')) should switch to the created field instead, since member_for is deprecated in Drupal 11.5 and will be removed in Drupal 13:

Summary

Drupal core has deprecated several procedural functions from the update.inc include file: update_check_requirements(), update_system_schema_requirements(), update_do_one(), and the internal _update_fix_missing_schema(). Their logic has moved to a new Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate service class. This is part of a longer-running effort to stop relying on manually included legacy .inc files and let the class autoloader handle this code instead. There is no behavioral change for site owners; this only affects developers and contrib/custom code that calls these functions directly.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: update_check_requirements(), update_system_schema_requirements(), update_do_one(), and _update_fix_missing_schema() in update.inc are deprecated in favor of methods on the new Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate service.
  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate autowired service providing getRequirements(), systemSchemaRequirements(), and doOne().

Technical details

The new Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate class (registered as an autowired service) exposes getRequirements(), systemSchemaRequirements(), doOne(), and an @internal fixMissingSchema() method, reproducing the logic that used to live in the standalone functions but using constructor-injected dependencies (UpdateHookRegistry, ModuleHandlerInterface, MessengerInterface, LoggerChannelFactoryInterface) instead of \Drupal::service() lookups. The old update.inc functions are now thin deprecated wrappers that trigger E_USER_DEPRECATED and delegate to \Drupal::service(DatabaseUpdate::class).

DbUpdateController was updated to take DatabaseUpdate and UpdateHookRegistry as (nullable, for backward-compatible construction) constructor arguments, using them internally instead of calling update_check_requirements() or \Drupal::service('update.update_hook_registry') directly. The batch operation that used to invoke the procedural update_do_one callback now calls the class method callable DatabaseUpdate::class . ':doOne'. This issue was scoped to the first three functions of update.inc; it is a followup to the "#2999721: [META] Deprecate the legacy include files before Drupal 9" effort, and further update.inc functions are handled in separate follow-up issues.

Upgrade

Replace direct calls to the deprecated update.inc functions with the new service:

// Before:
$requirements = update_check_requirements();
$schema_requirements = update_system_schema_requirements();
update_do_one($module, $number, $dependency_map, $context);

// After:
$requirements = \Drupal::service(\Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate::class)->getRequirements();
$schema_requirements = \Drupal::service(\Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate::class)->systemSchemaRequirements();
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate::class)->doOne($module, (int) $number, $dependency_map, $context);

_update_fix_missing_schema() has no direct public replacement; its logic is now DatabaseUpdate::fixMissingSchema(), which is marked @internal.

Any code constructing DbUpdateController directly should pass the new $databaseUpdate and $updateHookRegistry constructor arguments; omitting them still works but triggers a deprecation notice and will be required in Drupal 13.

item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core

  • Changes: 7 files, +231/−153 · php +226/−152 · js +4/−1 · txt +1

  • Followers: 23

Summary

Drupal has long supported "tabledrag": draggable table rows used for reordering things like block regions, menu items, or field weights. The logic that wires this behavior to a table (previously the procedural drupal_attach_tabledrag() function) has been moved into the Table form element as a proper static method, and the old function is now deprecated. This is part of the ongoing effort to remove procedural code from common.inc. Site builders and users won't notice any functional difference; draggable tables continue to work exactly as before. Module developers who called drupal_attach_tabledrag() directly (for example, custom admin tables with reorderable rows) should switch to the new method ahead of Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Tables using #tabledrag now render with an added tabledrag-enabled class and a data-drupal-tabledrag attribute; the JS no longer relies solely on the table's id.
  • Deprecation: drupal_attach_tabledrag() is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed in drupal:13.0.0; use \Drupal\Core\Render\Element\Table::attachTabledrag() instead.
  • New API: New public static method \Drupal\Core\Render\Element\Table::attachTabledrag() contains the logic formerly in drupal_attach_tabledrag().

Technical details

The function body of drupal_attach_tabledrag() in core/includes/common.inc was moved verbatim into a new public static method, \Drupal\Core\Render\Element\Table::attachTabledrag(), and the original function now just triggers an E_USER_DEPRECATED error and delegates to it. All core callers (Table::preRenderTable(), FieldUiTable::tablePreRender(), and the Views UI rearrange-filter form) were updated to call the new method directly.

As part of the move, the internal counter used to generate a unique tabledrag instance ID per table (previously stored via drupal_static()) was reworked twice during the issue's long history: first to a static class property, then, after concerns raised about correctness in the memory cache and long-running PHP contexts, to \Drupal::cache('memory') keyed by Table::TABLE_DRAG_CACHE_ID, so the counter doesn't get reset unexpectedly between requests handled by the same PHP process (e.g. FrankenPHP, RoadRunner). The table's HTML id is still printed for backward compatibility, but the internal selector used to wire up the JS behavior was switched from the raw id to a dedicated data-drupal-tabledrag attribute (plus a tabledrag-enabled class), and core/misc/tabledrag.js's once() selector was updated to match on [data-drupal-tabledrag="${base}"] instead of #${base}.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: February 24, 2019
  • Committed: September 11, 2026 (7 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • andypost (Skilld)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • finnsky (Skilld)
  • voleger (Drupal Ukraine Community)
  • naresh_bavaskar (QED42)
  • nod_ (Smile)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • daffie
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • claudiu.cristea (Webikon)
  • kim.pepper (PreviousNext)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)

Collaboration

This issue took over six years to land because of a substantive, recurring technical debate. Early on, claudiu.cristea and andypost argued over whether the new method should be called via self:: or static:: so subclasses could override just attachTabledrag() without duplicating preRenderTable(); claudiu.cristea's late-static-binding explanation (with a 3v4l.org example) settled it in favor of allowing proper overriding.

catch then pointed out that relying on an incrementing counter tied to a table's HTML id is unsafe with dynamic page cache, since two independently-cached blocks rendered in different requests could collide on the same ID, and proposed switching to a data-* attribute (issue #1090592 territory). nod_ significantly simplified the resulting JS patch, showing that only the once() selector needed to change, without new CSS classes or state-tracking. alexpott later caught a subtle off-by-one regression in the counter refactor (starting at 1 instead of 0) introduced by the static-property rewrite. Years later, catch re-raised the original concern that a static property still didn't solve the multi-request collision problem, and nicxvan and catch worked out the eventual fix: storing the counter in the memory cache bin instead of a static property.

Summary

The installer, update.php, and any early maintenance-mode pages (shown when the database or bootstrap is unavailable) now use the Admin theme (default_admin) instead of Claro. This is a step toward deprecating Claro. Distribution profiles that need a different installer theme can still request one via the distribution.install.theme key in their info file, and sites can still override the theme by setting $settings['maintenance_theme'] in settings.php.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: The maintenance_theme example in default.settings.php now shows default_admin instead of claro; sites that explicitly set $settings['maintenance_theme'] = 'claro'; keep working, but the out of the box default for install, update.php and early maintenance pages is now default_admin.
  • New API: New \Drupal\Core\Installer\InstallerKernel::INSTALL_THEME constant identifies the theme used for install, update, and early maintenance pages, replacing hardcoded 'claro' strings throughout core.

Technical details

The hardcoded 'claro' fallback used in install_state_defaults(), _drupal_maintenance_theme(), and InstallerKernel::getExtensions() was replaced with a new InstallerKernel::INSTALL_THEME constant ('default_admin'). InstallerKernel::getExtensions() was refactored into a new private getInstallThemes() helper that resolves the install theme (and its base themes, unless the theme is the default install theme, which declares base theme: false so no filesystem scan is needed) whether or not a profile has been selected yet.

A new InstallerKernel::updateThemes() override keeps the install theme's hook implementations registered throughout the whole install process: normally, installing a profile or recipe replaces the theme registry with just the themes the profile installed, which drops the install theme's hooks (Drupal\Core\Hook\ThemeHookCollectorPass) even though the install theme keeps rendering the remaining pages, including the final "configure site" step. This previously caused subtle breakage such as fonts not being preloaded and custom installer-theme hook implementations disappearing mid-install; both are now covered by new assertions in InstallerTest and test_installer_theme.

Other fixes needed to make default_admin usable during install: HtmlResponseAttachmentsProcessor::processAttachments() now uses $this->fileUrlGenerator->generateString() for preloaded fonts so the URL is root-relative instead of relative to install.php; default_admin's PreprocessHooks::preprocessHtml() now short-circuits toolbar/navigation class handling via InstallerKernel::installationAttempted() because permission checks need a database that does not exist yet during install; and default_admin\Settings::getAdminTheme() now returns ?string (falling back to the active theme) since system.theme configuration is unavailable during install.

item.description:

Summary

Exposed numeric and date range filters (the "between" operator, showing two input fields) previously always labeled their fields "Min" and "Max", which made little sense for a date range like "Authored on". Views now lets you configure these labels per filter, under "Minimum value label" and "Maximum value label" in the exposed filter settings. New filters default to "Minimum"/"Maximum" for numeric fields and "Start date"/"End date" for date fields; existing exposed filters keep showing "Min"/"Max" after upgrade so nothing changes visually unless you opt in.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Views numeric filter expose config gains min_label and max_label keys (defaults Minimum/Maximum, or Start date/End date for date filters); views_post_update_filter_min_max_labels() back-fills existing exposed filters with the legacy Min/Max labels so upgrading sites keep their current display.

Technical details

The change lives in NumericFilter and the date filter that extends it (views.filter.numeric/date schema in views.schema.yml). defineOptions() and defaultExposeOptions() add min_label/max_label to the expose array, and buildExposeForm() adds the two textfields (visible only when a two-value operator like "between" is selected, via the same #states used for the placeholder fields). valueForm() now sets $form['value']['min']['#title']/['max']['#title'] from $this->options['expose']['min_label']/max_label instead of the hardcoded t('Min')/t('Max').

Because this adds new config keys, ViewsConfigUpdater::needsMinMaxLabelUpdate()/processMinMaxLabelUpdate() and the views_post_update_filter_min_max_labels() post-update hook detect filters that already have min_placeholder (i.e. derive from NumericFilter) but lack min_label, and set both to the literal string Min/Max so upgraded sites render exactly as before. New views created after this change get the friendlier defaults instead.
